Chapter Two: Sparking Motivation—Understanding Others’ Desires and Interests.
Now that we’ve laid down a foundation of respect and appreciation, let’s take things a step further. If you really want to influence someone, you’ve got to get curious about what drives them. Everyone’s got their own hopes, needs, and ambitions—and the real magic happens when you start to see things from their point of view.
Instead of trying to convince someone by sheer logic or pushing your own agenda, what if you could tap into what already matters to them? It starts with listening—really listening. Ask thoughtful questions, and notice what lights them up or, on the flip side, what makes them hesitate. When people feel seen and heard, you’ll find they’re not only more open, but actually want to engage.
Think about a coworker who seems reluctant to take on a new project. You could list all the reasons it’s good for the team, but there’s a better way. What if you took a moment to find out what’s important to them? Maybe they’re looking for new challenges, a chance to shine, or a bit more creative freedom. If you can frame the project around what they value, suddenly it’s not just another task—it’s an opportunity that speaks directly to them.
This approach works in all kinds of situations. Whether you’re a parent encouraging your child to study, a salesperson introducing a product, or a friend offering support—the secret is to focus less on your own goals, and more on what the other person cares about.
So, how can you spark real motivation? Here are a few practical steps:
First, get genuinely interested in what others want or value. Second, whenever you make a request or suggestion, try to frame it in terms of their interests—not just yours. And finally, invite people to talk about their own goals, dreams, and concerns.
When you do this, you’re not just making it easier to get a yes—you’re also building trust and connection. People love to feel respected and understood, and when they do, they’re far more likely to step up, collaborate, and say yes to working with you.
